lines: Welcome to Module Six: Prompt Engineering.
It's about getting more out of a model without touching its weights.
Picture an IT team building an assistant for their internal runbooks.
There's no training budget, so fine-tuning is off the table.

say.0: Picture an I T team building an assistant for their internal runbooks.

lines: Their first attempt is a one-line prompt.
The model rambles, invents a server name, and returns broken JSON.

say.1: The model rambles, invents a server name, and returns broken jason.

lines: None of that needs new weights.
It needs a better prompt, better decoding, and the right documents.
Lesson one starts with in-context learning.
A frozen model picks up a task from examples in its prompt, with no gradient update.
Zero-shot gives just the instruction, while few-shot adds worked examples.
How you choose and order those examples matters more than you'd expect.
Chat models expect system, user, and assistant roles.
The chat template turns them into the tokens the model was trained on.
Lesson two makes the model reason before it answers.
Chain-of-thought asks for steps, and self-consistency samples several chains and votes.
Then you'll control how each token is picked.
Temperature reshapes probabilities, while top-k and top-p trim the unlikely tail.

say.1: Temperature reshapes probabilities, while top K and top P trim the unlikely tail.

lines: In a short lab, you'll run one prompt under different settings.
Seeds, stop sequences, and token limits make results repeatable.
For the tickets, asking nicely for JSON isn't enough.
Constrained decoding in vLLM only allows tokens that keep the output schema-valid.

say.0: For the tickets, asking nicely for jason isn't enough.
say.1: Constrained decoding in V L L M only allows tokens that keep the output schema valid.

lines: Lesson three adds your own documents with retrieval-augmented generation, or RAG.
You'll chunk runbooks, embed them, and index them with FAISS.

lines: At question time, the closest chunks are retrieved, reranked, and cited in the prompt.
Mixing keyword and dense search catches exact names and paraphrases alike.
NVIDIA's NeMo Retriever serves embedding and reranking models as NIM microservices.
Grounding instructions and citations keep answers tied to sources.

lines: Now the assistant answers from the runbook, cites it, and returns valid JSON.
And when nothing relevant is found, it says it doesn't know.

lines: By the end, you'll build a RAG pipeline and know when to prompt, retrieve, or fine-tune.
